items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The sun is the center of our solar system. Eight planets orbit the sun. Planets closer to the sun are rocky. Planets farther from the sun are large and made of gas.

Image: A diagram shows the sun on the left and eight planets lined up to the right. The first four are small gray and brown circles. The last four are much larger circles colored tan, yellow, blue, and blue-green.

Explain how the image and text work together to explain the solar system. What does the image show that the text alone does not, and what does the text explain that you cannot get from the image alone?
items.answer: The text and image work together to give a complete picture of the solar system. The text explains the rule that close planets are rocky and far planets are gas giants. The image shows this rule visually by making the first four planets small and dark and the last four noticeably bigger and colorful. From the image alone you could see size differences but not understand why. From the text alone you could understand the rule but not see what it looks like. Together, the rule from the text is proven by the visual pattern in the image.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

A seed needs the right conditions to sprout. Soil provides nutrients. Water softens the seed coat so roots can push through. Warmth speeds up the sprouting process.

Image: A diagram shows a seed underground with three labeled arrows pointing toward it: an arrow from above labeled 'warmth from sun,' an arrow from the side labeled 'water,' and an arrow from below labeled 'nutrients from soil.' A small green sprout points upward from the seed.

A student says: 'The image shows the same information as the text, so looking at both is not necessary.' Do you agree or disagree? Explain your thinking.
items.answer: I disagree. The text and image each add something the other does not. The text explains what each condition does, for example water softens the seed coat. The image shows where each condition comes from (sun above, water from the side, nutrients from below) and shows the result with a growing sprout. A reader who only looks at the image knows what is needed but not why each condition helps. A reader who only reads the text knows the reasons but cannot picture how the seed receives each ingredient. Both together give the fullest understanding.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Magnets attract some metals but not others. Iron and steel are attracted to magnets. Aluminum and copper are not. A magnet has two poles, a north pole and a south pole. Opposite poles attract each other.

Image: A diagram shows two bar magnets. In the first picture, the north pole of one magnet faces the south pole of another. Arrows between them point toward each other labeled 'attract.' In the second picture, two north poles face each other. Arrows point away from each other labeled 'repel.'

The text talks about which metals magnets attract. The image shows something different. What does the image show that is not in the text, and why is that information important?
items.answer: The image shows that two magnets can either attract or repel each other depending on which poles are facing, which is not described in the text at all. The text only mentions that opposite poles attract, but it does not explain what happens when the same poles face each other. The image adds the concept of repulsion and shows both situations visually with labeled arrows. This information is important because it shows that magnets interact with each other in two different ways, not just one.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The layers of the rainforest each support different kinds of life. The emergent layer at the top gets the most sunlight. The canopy below it is thick with leaves. The understory is shadier. The forest floor is darkest of all.

Image: A diagram shows a side view of a rainforest. At the very top are a few tall trees poking above everything labeled 'emergent layer.' Below that is a dense green roof of treetops labeled 'canopy.' Lower still are smaller trees in shade labeled 'understory.' At the bottom is dark soil with mushrooms labeled 'forest floor.'

How does the image help you understand why different animals live in different layers? Use information from both the text and the image in your answer.
items.answer: The text explains that each layer gets a different amount of sunlight, from most at the top to least at the bottom. The image makes this clear by showing how the canopy forms a thick roof that blocks light from reaching the lower layers, which is why the understory and forest floor look darker. An animal that needs sunlight would live in the emergent layer or canopy, while an animal that does well in shade or darkness would live lower. Together, the text and image show that the amount of sunlight in each layer determines which animals and plants can survive there.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Lightning forms during a thunderstorm. Ice crystals and water droplets inside storm clouds crash together and build up electric charge. The bottom of the cloud becomes negatively charged. The ground below becomes positively charged. When the difference is large enough, electricity jumps from cloud to ground as a bolt of lightning.

Image: A diagram shows a dark storm cloud. Inside, plus and minus signs are scattered. The bottom of the cloud is covered in minus signs. Below the cloud, the ground is covered in plus signs. A jagged bright line goes from the cloud to the ground labeled 'lightning bolt.'

Explain how the signs in the diagram work together with the text to explain lightning. What would be hard to understand from the text alone that the image makes clear?
items.answer: The text explains that the bottom of the cloud becomes negatively charged and the ground becomes positively charged, and when the difference is large enough, lightning jumps between them. The image uses plus and minus signs to show exactly where the charges build up. Without the image, it is hard to picture what 'negatively charged' and 'positively charged' mean in a physical space. The diagram makes it clear that the charges are opposite and that they are lined up facing each other (cloud bottom to ground), which explains why the electricity jumps across that specific gap. The combination of the explanation in the text and the visual of the charges in the image is needed to fully understand why lightning goes from cloud to ground.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Honeybees communicate with each other by dancing. When a bee finds flowers, it returns to the hive and does a waggle dance. The angle of the dance tells other bees which direction to fly. The length of the dance tells them how far away the flowers are.

Image: A diagram shows a bee dancing in a figure-eight pattern inside the hive. An arrow inside the middle of the figure eight points at a 45-degree angle upward to the right, labeled 'direction to flowers.' A clock symbol in the corner shows a short time labeled 'nearby' and a long time labeled 'far away.'

A classmate says the image is not needed because the text already explains how bees dance. Do you agree or disagree? Give two specific reasons using details from both the text and the image.
items.answer: I disagree. The image adds two things the text does not. First, the text says the angle of the dance gives direction, but seeing the figure-eight pattern with an actual arrow at 45 degrees makes it much easier to understand what 'angle' means in the context of a bee dance. Without the image, it is hard to picture what direction information looks like in a dance. Second, the clock symbol in the image shows how time and distance relate, which the text mentions but does not visualize. The image turns abstract descriptions of angle and length into something you can actually see and measure, which is important for truly understanding how bee communication works.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Tsunami waves look small in the open ocean. The water can be only about one meter high but the wave stretches for hundreds of kilometers below the surface. When the wave reaches shallow water near the coast, the underwater part cannot move forward, so the water piles up into a giant wall.

Image: Two diagrams are shown side by side. The left diagram shows the open ocean with a tiny wave on the surface and a huge triangle of water below the surface labeled 'tsunami underwater.' The right diagram shows the same wave reaching a beach. The underwater part is now compressed and the surface wave is enormous, labeled 'tsunami at shore.'

Explain how the image and text work together to explain why tsunamis are dangerous at shore but not in the open ocean. What does each one contribute that the other cannot?
items.answer: The text explains the reason behind the danger: in the open ocean the energy is spread out over a huge underwater area, but near shore the underwater water cannot move forward so all that energy piles up into a tall wave. The image contributes what the text cannot describe well in words: it shows the enormous difference in size between the tiny surface ripple in the open ocean and the towering wave at shore. The side-by-side comparison makes the transformation visually dramatic and easy to see. Without the text, a reader seeing the images would not understand why the wave changes. Without the images, a reader would struggle to picture how a small wave could become so enormous. Together they create a full explanation of both what happens and why.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The Grand Canyon was formed over millions of years by the Colorado River. The river slowly carved through layers of rock. Each layer of rock is a different age. The oldest rocks are at the bottom and the youngest are at the top.

Image: A diagram shows a side view of the Grand Canyon. The walls of the canyon are made of horizontal stripes of different colors. Starting from the bottom: dark gray rock labeled '1.7 billion years old,' then red-brown rock, then tan rock, then pale yellow rock at the top labeled '270 million years old.' A thin blue line at the bottom shows the Colorado River.

How do the rock layers in the image help you understand what the text means when it says the canyon tells the story of Earth's history? Use both the text and the image in your answer.
items.answer: The text says each rock layer is a different age and the oldest rocks are at the bottom. The image shows this visually by using different colors for each layer and labeling them with actual ages. When you see that the bottom layer is 1.7 billion years old and the top layer is 270 million years old, the idea that the canyon tells Earth's history becomes concrete. Each colored stripe in the diagram is like a page of Earth's history, and the deeper you go the further back in time you go. The image turns an abstract idea about deep time into something you can see as a stack of colored bands, which makes the text's claim about history feel real and understandable.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Air pressure changes with altitude. At sea level, the weight of all the air above presses down heavily. As you climb higher, there is less air above you, so pressure decreases. This is why climbers at high altitudes need oxygen tanks.

Image: A diagram shows a mountain from base to peak. At the base, many closely spaced dots represent air molecules and a scale reads 'high pressure.' Halfway up, the dots are more spread out and the scale reads 'medium pressure.' Near the peak, there are very few dots and the scale reads 'low pressure.'

A student looks only at the image and says: 'This diagram shows that mountains have less air at the top than at the bottom.' Is that a complete explanation? What does the text add that makes the explanation more complete?
items.answer: The student's statement is accurate but incomplete. The image clearly shows that air molecules are more spread out near the mountain peak, which does mean there is less air. However, the text adds the explanation of why this happens: because there is less air above you as you go higher, there is less weight pressing down, so pressure is lower. The text also explains a consequence the image does not show: that low pressure means climbers need oxygen tanks. The image shows the pattern (less air higher up) while the text explains the cause (weight of air above) and a real-world effect (need for oxygen). Together they create a full explanation rather than just a description.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Deforestation is the cutting down of large areas of forest. When forests are cut, animals lose their habitat. Tree roots that once held soil in place are gone, so rain washes the soil away in a process called erosion. Without trees, the land becomes dry and bare.

Image: Two side-by-side photos are shown. The left photo shows a lush green forest with tall trees, thick undergrowth, and a stream with clear water. The right photo shows the same area after deforestation: bare brown ground, muddy water in the stream, and no trees or plants.

Explain how the before-and-after photos work together with the text to show the consequences of deforestation. What does the image prove that the text claims, and what does the text explain that the image alone cannot tell you?
items.answer: The text makes three claims: animals lose habitat, soil erodes, and the land becomes dry and bare. The before-and-after photos prove two of these visually. The left photo shows a healthy forest with a clear stream, and the right photo shows bare ground with muddy water, proving erosion has occurred. The disappearance of plants in the right photo also proves the land becomes bare. However, the image cannot explain why the water becomes muddy or why the land is bare. The text provides those explanations by telling readers that tree roots held soil in place and that without trees the land dries out. The photos make the consequences feel real and visible, while the text explains the causes behind what the photos show.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Bats navigate in the dark using echolocation. They send out high-pitched sounds that bounce off objects and return to the bat's ears. By listening to the echoes, a bat can tell how far away something is and whether it is moving.

Image: A diagram shows a bat on the left. Curved lines spread outward from the bat's mouth labeled 'sound waves.' The lines hit a small moth in the center and bounce back toward the bat labeled 'echo.'

A classmate says the image on its own completely explains echolocation without needing to read the text. Do you agree or disagree? Explain what each one contributes.
items.answer: I disagree. The image shows the path of sound waves going out and echoes coming back, which makes the physical process visible. However, the image cannot explain that the bat listens to the echoes to judge distance and movement. Without the text, a reader might understand that sound bounces back but not know that the bat uses the echo to gather information about its surroundings. The text explains the purpose and the result of echolocation (knowing distance and movement), while the image shows the mechanism (sound traveling out and echoes returning). Both are needed for a complete understanding.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

The water in a river moves at different speeds in different parts of the river. In the center, water moves fastest because there is little friction. Near the banks and river bottom, water is slowed by friction from rocks and soil.

Image: A diagram shows a river from above. In the center, long arrows point downstream labeled 'fast.' Near the banks, short arrows point downstream labeled 'slow.'

How do the arrows in the image help clarify the scientific concept of friction that the text describes?
items.answer: The text explains that friction from the riverbanks and bottom slows water near the edges. The image makes this concept visible by using long arrows in the center (showing fast movement) and short arrows near the banks (showing slow movement). Without the image, friction is an abstract idea. With the image, readers can see exactly where fast and slow water are located and that the difference is dramatic. The arrows also show that the water is all moving in the same direction, which clarifies that friction changes speed but not direction. Together, the image turns the scientific explanation in the text into something you can see and measure by arrow length.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

A simple machine called a lever can help you lift heavy things. A lever is a stiff bar that rests on a point called a fulcrum. When you push down on one end, the other end goes up. The position of the fulcrum changes how much force you need.

Image: Two diagrams are shown. In the first, the fulcrum is close to the heavy object. The effort arrow on the far end is very long, labeled 'less force needed.' In the second, the fulcrum is in the middle. The effort arrow is shorter, labeled 'more force needed.'

What does the image reveal about levers that is only hinted at in the text? Why is this information important for understanding how levers work?
items.answer: The text says the position of the fulcrum changes how much force is needed, but it does not explain the relationship clearly. The image reveals the specific rule: when the fulcrum is close to the heavy object, you need less force, but when the fulcrum is in the middle, you need more force. The long and short arrows make this difference immediately visible. This is important because it tells users of levers exactly where to place the fulcrum to make lifting easiest. Without the image, the text's hint about fulcrum position would be vague and hard to apply in practice.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Salt water and fresh water have different densities. Salt water is denser than fresh water. When salt water and fresh water meet in an estuary, the denser salt water sinks below the lighter fresh water. This creates two layers of water in the same body.

Image: A diagram shows a cross-section of an estuary where a river meets the ocean. Blue arrows on top represent fresh water flowing toward the ocean. Dark blue arrows at the bottom represent salt water pushing in from the ocean. The two layers are labeled with their directions.

Explain how the two-layer diagram proves the scientific claim in the text. What would a reader miss without the image?
items.answer: The text claims that denser salt water sinks below lighter fresh water in an estuary. The diagram proves this by showing the two layers as arrows flowing in opposite directions at different levels: fresh water flows on top toward the ocean and salt water flows on the bottom pushing inland. Seeing the arrows at different depths proves the layering the text describes. Without the image, a reader would have to imagine this invisible underwater process happening inside what looks like a single body of water. The image makes the invisible visible and confirms that the two water types do not mix but instead form distinct layers moving in different directions.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Circadian rhythms are the body's internal clock. They follow a roughly 24-hour cycle. In the morning, the body releases hormones that increase energy. In the afternoon, body temperature peaks. In the evening, the body starts releasing melatonin to prepare for sleep.

Image: A circular clock diagram is shown. Starting at 6 a.m. going clockwise: 'wake up, hormones rise' at 6 a.m.; 'peak body temperature' at 3 p.m.; 'melatonin released' at 9 p.m.; 'deep sleep' at midnight; and back to 6 a.m.

Explain why a circular diagram is especially well-suited to representing circadian rhythms. What does the circular shape add beyond what the text provides?
items.answer: The circular shape is especially fitting because it shows that circadian rhythms are a cycle that repeats every 24 hours, not a sequence that ends. The text lists events in order (morning, afternoon, evening) but describes them as if they are a linear series of events. The circular diagram shows that after deep sleep at midnight the cycle returns to 6 a.m., making the repeating nature of the rhythm visually obvious. This shape adds the meaning that the body never really stops cycling. The text would need extra explanation to convey the same idea, while the circle communicates it instantly through its shape alone.
